findings.location: 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost-synthesis.pdf p. 2 (every full-width explanatory and event row of the Scriptural Date and Location dossier) and 57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf pp. 33-34 (the same rows in the terminal dossier); set by \dossierprose and \dossierevent in src/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost/format.tex
findings.problem: The spanning explanatory and event rows are set in \scriptsize (about 8pt on an 11pt base) across 0.98\linewidth, which yields lines of roughly 115-125 characters -- by some margin the smallest type on the longest measure anywhere in the three documents. The glyphs themselves are clean and legible at print size, and the leaf documents the reduction as deliberate deviation D2 taken so that all seven dossiers stand on the single physical page the concise contract fixes for page 2, which the 1962 profile's own clause on changing measurements permits. But the profile fixes that spanning row at 0.92\linewidth, and the leaf widened rather than narrowed it, so the one setting in the production that most taxes the eye is also the one that moved furthest from the fixed measure in the direction that hurts reading.
findings.required_result: The dossier's full-width explanatory and event rows carry no more than about 100 characters per line at their present size -- for example by returning the spanning row to the profile's 0.92\linewidth, or by indenting it under the summary tier -- while the complete seven-dossier inventory still occupies exactly physical page 2 of the concise PDF, page 2 still carries nothing else, and no evidence is dropped from any dossier. If no such setting keeps all seven dossiers on one page, the present measurement stands and the reason is recorded beside deviation D2 in format.tex.

observations.note: The homily's PDF catalog declares /PageMode/UseOutlines but carries no /Outlines object, so a viewer that honours the page mode opens an empty bookmark pane; the study and the concise study both carry real outline trees alongside the same page mode. The homily is five pages and needs no bookmarks to be navigable, and my lane's criteria ask for navigation only of the study, so this is noted rather than raised.

summary: Independent full-page visual review of all three sealed artifacts of liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost, each rasterised afresh from the sealed bytes (pdftoppm 26.08.0 / ImageMagick 7.1.2-31, 200 dpi full pages plus contact sheets) and inspected page by page, not by contact sheet alone. Reviewed artifacts, receipt hashes recomputed and matching REVIEW_INPUTS exactly, with page coverage: build/claude/.../57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.pdf sha256 a5705241a178bc453e6a93c23f9f6e9201faac8630361470830e51b839dc05d5, 38 physical pages, pages 1-38 all inspected at full size; build/claude/.../57-seventeenth-after-pentecost-synthesis.pdf sha256 126bf160fb5de7e936399c24396d8bc93b46126e736e5f2d0b0a348591959dd7, 12 physical pages, pages 1-12 all inspected at full size; build/claude/.../57-seventeenth-after-pentecost-homily.pdf sha256 923fb4936d107d3dec13fc6cf1b7a9197aed5dbb1ef19ae20cc5bb8f2d2fb289, 5 physical pages, pages 1-5 all inspected at full size. Pagination evidence verified against the seal (57-...aux b9c43bb6..., 57-...log a58761f7..., 57-...-synthesis.aux e2b03c30..., 57-...-synthesis.log 86221563...), and all 25 render_inputs in research/artifacts.json rehashed and matching. Extent: study 38 pages (20-50 required), concise 12 pages (10-12 required). Concise restored opening verified against the settled zref-abspage markers and against the actual rasters, which agree exactly: inventory start/end and overview start/end with all four sense markers (literal, allegorical, moral, anagogical) on abspage 1; chronology start/end on abspage 2; themes start abspage 3, end abspage 4; commentary start abspage 5. Page 1 carries the complete ten-element map in liturgical order (introit, collect, epistle, gradual, alleluia, gospel, offertory, secret, communion, postcommunion, matching proper-components.toml element_keys) with the rubrical note on class, colour, Gloria, Credo, single oration set and Trinity Preface, followed by exactly four overview rows; page 2 carries Scriptural Date and Location alone, complete at seven distinct passages (Ps 32, 75, 101, 118, Dan 9, Mt 22, Eph 4) in canonical then verse order, readable; pages 3-4 are substantively filled argument (measured body fill 0.98 and 0.96 of the text block) with no forced break into unused space; page 5 opens genuine interleaved commentary organised by cross-proper questions, not by successive lane summaries. Composition checks: 11pt Pagella on 15pt leading over a ~70-character measure in both studies, 12.5pt on 17pt unjustified with block paragraphs in the spoken homily; consistent heading hierarchy; running heads (Sunday left, current section right) and centred folios on every page except the three terminal colophon pages, whose empty page style is the shared preamble's documented behaviour; all fonts embedded and subsetted (TeX Gyre Pagella roman/bold/italic/bold-italic plus LM Mono) in all three PDFs; no Overfull or Underfull box, no LaTeX or package warning and no headheight warning in any of the three logs; the custom versicle glyph renders correctly; measured ink boxes show no content clipped into or past the 1.3in side margins beyond normal microtype protrusion, and no overlapping content anywhere. Table integrity verified on the study's inventory (p. 3), three-reading comparison (p. 31) and two-page dossier (pp. 33-34, header repeated on the continuation, each dossier's summary row kept with its explanatory row) and on the concise map, overview and dossier tables; column gutters are tight in places but nowhere collide. No conspicuous blank page and no padding: every partly filled page in the study (pp. 1, 3, 13, 19, 32, 33, 34, 38) is a title page, a section-start clearpage, a keep-together table break or the colophon page, and the concise study has no partly filled page at all. The homily's spoken body runs pp. 1-3 with no inline apparatus, headings or stage directions; the Note on Sources and Delivery and the References stand after a clearpage on pp. 4-5, so source notes are present without intruding into the speech. Meaningful limits of this review: it judges rendered pages, not source support, theological coherence or the truth of any claim, which belong to the content and research reviews; PDF text extraction and log inspection supplement but do not replace the page inspection; and the pre-existing contact sheets already in the tree were rendered from a superseded homily PDF, so they were not relied on. Verdict: PASS, with one advisory on the dossier explanatory-row measure and two observations.
